digest.component_or_area: outbound parent hierarchy sync (CREATE emit and ACLI attach fallback)
propositions: CREATE emit path (_map_local_to_jira_fields:145-156) silently drops a bound non-epic parent without recording a bridge alert, leaving only a debug log line invisible to operators.
ACLI attach fallback (_attach_parent_guarded:136-143) swallows an HTTP 400 rejection from the tracker and returns success, with no durable record of the parent divergence.

The epic-only parent guard is unconditional and documented as a universal standard project constraint, but its justification (next-gen Jira 400s non-epic parents) does not apply to Data Center, which silently accept-and-ignores such parents instead.

The project's contract (stated in pass_io.py and dispatch_one.py) requires a durable operator-visible record (bridge_alerts entry) for any parent that cannot reach the tracker; ticket 39c1 and change 9f26 wired this into two of four surfaces, leaving slots 2 and 4 exposed.

An unbound parent (not yet synced to the tracker) must remain silent on drop, because it converges on a later pass and alerting on it produces churn, distinguishing it from a bound parent whose drop is a real loss.
